court: In the High Court of Madras
advocates: For Respondents: Mr. G. Jeremiah for RR 1 to 3
Mr. G. Harihara Arun Soma Sankar Govt. Advocate (Crl. Side) for R 4
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

P. Velmurugan, J.:— This criminal revision case has been filed seeking to set aside the reversal judgment of acquittal made by the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Vellore, in C.A. No. 158 of 2011 dated 25.08.2012, reversing the judgment of conviction made by the learned Assistant Sessions Judge-cum-Chief Judicial Magistrate, Vellore, in S.C. No. 313 of 2010 dated 12.07.2011.

2. The fourth respondent police registered a case against the respondents 1 to 7 based on the complaint given by the revision petitioner in Cr. No. 381 of 2010 for the offence punishable under Sections 294(b), 307 against 1st respondent/A1 and 307 r/w 34 of IPC against 2nd & 3rd respondents/A2 & A3. After completing investigation, the fourth respondent police laid a charge sheet before the learned Judicial Magistrate I, Vellore, and the charge sheet was taken on file in P.R.C. No. 18 of 2010. The learned Judicial Magistrate, since the offence charged against the accused was triable by the Court of Sessions committed the same to the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Vellore, and in turn the same was made over to the learned Assistant Sessions Judge-cum-Chief Judicial Magistrate, Vellore.

3. Before the trial Court, in order prove the case of the prosecution, P.Ws.1 to 10 were examined and Exs.P1 to 9 were marked besides five material objects. On the side of the defence, no one was examined and Exs.D1 & 2 were marked. The learned Assistant Sessions Judge-cum-Chief Judicial Magistrate, Vellore, after trial found all the accused guilty for the offence under Section 324 of IPC and by judgment dated 12.07.2011, convicted all the accused and sentenced them to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of six months each with fine of Rs. 1,000/- each, in default, to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a further period of two weeks. Aggrieved against the judgment of conviction, all the accused had preferred appeal before the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Vellore, in C.A. No. 158 of 2011. The learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Vellore, after hearing both the counsel and perusing the records, acquitted the respondents 1 to 3/accused. Challenging the reversal judgment of acquittal made by the lower appellate Court, the defacto complainant/P.W.6 is before this Court with the present criminal revision.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that due to civil dispute between the parties, on 07.06.2010 respondents 1 to 3 had entered in Brick Klin belonging to the petitioner and not allowed to load the bricks in the lorry and when the petitioner arrived at the spot, all the accused had abused him in a filthy language and attacked with knife and caused injuries. The Doctor/P.W.5 has clearly spoken about the injuries sustained by the petitioner/victim. Even though, initially P.Ws.1 & 2 not supported the case of the prosecution, on recall, the above witnesses had clearly stated about the facts and corroborated the evidence of the defacto complainant/P.W.6. The trial Court has rightly appreciated the evidence and convicted the respondents 1 to 3, but the lower appellate has miserably failed to consider the evidence of prosecution witnesses and erroneously acquitted the respondents 1 to 3, which warrants serious interference.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the respondents 1 to 3 would submit that except P.W.6, none of the prosecution witnesses had supported the case of the prosecution. The petitioner and the respondents 1 to 3 are brothers and due to some civil dispute the alleged occurrence had taken place. Further the respondents 1 & 3 have also sustained injuries in the same occurrence and the Investigating Officer/P.W.9 has also admitted the injuries sustained by the accused. The respondents 1 to 3 had lodged a counter complaint, which was not properly investigated by 4th respondent police and was closed as referred charge sheet. The injuries alleged to have been sustained by P.W.6 in the occurrence was not tallied with the medical records and the Doctor, who treated the petitioner, had opined that the injuries sustained by P.W.6 is only simple in nature. The injuries sustained by the accused was not properly explained by the prosecution. Therefore, even though, the trial Court convicted the respondents 1 to 3, the lower appellate has rightly come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and acquitted the respondents 1 to 3, which does not call for any interference.

6. The learned Government Advocate (Crl. Side) appearing for the respondent police would submit that based on the complaint given by the petitioner/P.W.6, case was registered and after trial the learned Magistrate convicted the respondents 1 to 3, but, the lower appellate Court has acquitted the respondents 1 to 3, on the ground of non explanation of the injuries sustained by the accused is fatal to the case of the prosecution. The respondent police, after investigating the complaint given by the accused had filed referred charge sheet and when the eye witnesses and the Doctor has clearly spoken about the injuries sustained by the petitioner/P.W.6, which corroborates with the medical records, non explanation of the injuries alleged to have been sustained by the accused will not affect the case of the prosecution.

7. Heard the learned counsel appearing on either side and carefully perused the materials placed on record and the judgments passed by both the Courts below.

8. It is seen that petitioner and the respondents 1 to 3 are brothers and based on the complaint lodged by the petitioner/P.W.6, case was registered against the respondents 1 to 3 for the offence punishable under Sections 294(b), 307 against 1st respondent/A1 and 307 r/w 34 of IPC against 2nd & 3rd respondents/A2 & A3 and the trial Court convicted all the accused, but, the lower appellate Court has acquitted them and against which, defacto complainant has preferred this revision. Due to land dispute, when the customers of the petitioner went to buy the bricks, they were wrongfully restrained by the respondents 1 to 3 and not allowed them to take the bricks and when P.W.6 reached his brick klin and questioned the act of the respondents 1 to 3, they all picked up quarrel and attacked P.W.6 and caused injuries. It is the case of the defence that the accused 1 & 3 also sustained injuries and the same has not been explained by the prosecution and further the case in counter has also been filed, but the same was closed as referred charge sheet by the respondent police. It is admitted by P.Ws.8 & 9, the Investigating Officers, in cross examination, that the complaint given by the accused was registered and later the same was closed as referred charge sheet. The respondents 1 to 3 did not take any effective steps to agitate their grievance, if they really suffered, either they should have filed protest petition or at least private complaint against the petitioner, but, they simply kept quite. The lower appellate Court has given finding that prosecution has not explained the injuries sustained by the accused.

9. Evidence of P.W.5, the Doctor, who admitted P.W.6 in the Hospital and issued wound certificate Ex.P2 and also copy of Accident Register shows that P.W.6 was attacked by three men with stick and knife and no where it was stated by P.W.6 that the accused also sustained injuries. It is seen in the proceedings under 313 Cr. P.C., respondents 1 to 3/accused had not stated anything about the injuries sustained by them and simply stated that they have not committed any offence. When questioning under 313 proceedings, A1 has answered that when P.W.6 attacked his brother, he prevented the same and at that time P.W.6 bite him and further A1, the first respondent herein has not denied the occurrence and he also stated that he has witness to examine, but he did not examine any witness. A2, the second respondent, while answering for the questions under 313 of Cr. P.C., has stated that he prevented from attacking A3 and falsely he was also implicated. Therefore, as far as occurrence is concerned, it has been proved, and there are witnesses available for the defence, as per the evidence the respondents 1 to 3/accused, but they failed to examine those witnesses. None of the accused had stated that P.W.6 ony is the aggressor and he only attacked and the accused did not take any effective steps to pursue their remedy against the closure of their complaint by the respondent police. In the absence of the above, the respondents 1 to 3/A1 to A3 are liable to be punished. The trial Court has rightly appreciated the evidence of prosecution as well as the deposition of the accused and convicted them, whereas, the lower appellate Court acquitted the respondents 1 to 3. On reading of evidence of P.Ws.1 to 3, 5 and 6, prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and therefore this Court is inclined to set aside the judgment of acquittal made by the lower appellate court and restore the judgment of conviction recorded by the trial Court.

10. Accordingly, this criminal revision case stands allowed and the judgment of acquittal made by the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Vellore, in C.A. No. 158 of 2011 dated 25.08.2012, is hereby set aside and judgment of conviction made in S.C. No. 313 of 2010 dated 12.07.2011 passed by the learned Assistant Sessions Judge-cum-Chief Judicial Magistrate, Vellore, is hereby restored. Trial Court is directed to secure the accused, to undergo remaining period of sentence imposed by the trial Court.
